l: A. A conflict of interest arises whenever an employee disregards the public interest in favor of other interests such as personal, family or business relationships. A conflict may exist whenever an employee, because of one of these relationships, is incapable of impartially performing their official duties. A conflict of interest may result in favorable or unfavorable actions whenever decisions are based on personal, family or business relationships. TBP 2.12

B. It is particularly important that conflicts between command/supervision and subordinates are avoided, especially within the same chain of command or workgroup. The authority given a supervisor over a subordinate is a responsibility entrusted to that supervisor by the Chief of Police which requires that every decision made by the supervisor be totally objective, impeccably fair, and above all, devoid of any favorable or unfavorable actions due to any relationship between the supervisor and the subordinate. Also, when a supervisor has a personal, family or business relationship with a subordinate, the relationships may result in a negative perception by others and the motive for decisions made by the supervisor may become suspect, compromising the integrity of all involved. This could lead to a disruptive work environment, reduced productivity and a decline in overall morale.

C. Staffing issues may result from family relationships between employees within the same workgroup, especially when employees take lengthy vacations together or when excessive discretionary days are simultaneously taken. Family relationships can also pose a serious dilemma in situations where employees may be required to testify against each other in criminal or civil cases and may result in poor decisions made by one employee during high stress incidents involving the other employee.
1. For purposes of this order, a supervisor is defined as a person who has command or supervision over others.
2. For purposes of this order, workgroup includes a division, section, district, or unit.

3. A supervisor/subordinate work relationship exists when, within the chain of command or workgroup, one employee commands, controls, directs, supervises, or may influence another employee’s terms, conditions or privileges of employment.
4. A personal relationship means a sexual, romantic, or dating relationship or any interpersonal relationship in which there is a non-platonic interest between two (2) employees.

5. A family relationship means immediate family such as spouse, child, stepchild, parent, stepparent, grandparent, grandparent-in-law, grandchild, parent-in-law, brother, sister, brother or sister-in-law, and son or daughter-in-law. A family relationship also includes employees who are romantically involved and cohabitating.

6. A business relationship means any association of two (2) or more persons to carry on a business for profit; the association of two (2) or more persons to own and/or to operate a business venture as equal members; two (2) or more persons who have a financial or pecuniary interest, directly or indirectly, in a business, service, or contract; or, any employee of the department who is employed directly or indirectly with any company or individual that does or seeks to do business with the city

E. When any employee believes a conflict exists or may exist due to personal, family or business reasons, the employee shall immediately contact their immediate supervisor or commander. The supervisor or commander contacted will resolve the situation in accordance with the provisions of this order.

F. Employees may report a relationship that potentially creates a conflict to an immediate supervisor, or the matter to any ascending-level supervisor in the officer’s chain of command, the police chaplain, or the female employees coordinator. The person receiving the information shall immediately report the matter to the appropriate Assistant Chief or the Chief of Police.

G. Supervisors making personnel assignments or selecting personnel for in-house vacancies shall not assign or select any employee for an assignment in which a personal, family or business relationship exists.

items.t: PERSONAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN A SUPERVISOR AND SUBORDINATE
l: A. A personal relationship between employees in and of itself is not inappropriate. The department shall exercise due respect for the right of personal associations and privacy of all employees of this organization. However, all decisions by a supervisor must be viewed as fair, objective, and impartial. Therefore, when personal relationships between supervisors and subordinates that create a conflict occur in the workplace, there is cause for concern by the department. These relationships must be addressed and resolved as directed by this order in the interest of maintaining an objective and impartial working environment for all employees. TBP 2.12
1. Supervisors shall not maintain or continue in a personal relationship with a subordinate within a two-rank separation in their chain of command or workgroup.
a. An example for separation would be one individual is a rank of officer and another is the rank of captain.

2. When a personal relationship exists or occurs between a supervisor and subordinate who are in the same chain of command or within the same workgroup that violates General Order 706.02 A1, the involved supervisor shall immediately inform their immediate supervisor. The appropriate division commander or manager shall also be notified and shall ensure one of the involved employees is immediately reassigned to a position in which the supervisor/subordinate relationship conflict no longer exists. The bureau Assistant Chief shall be notified to ensure the action taken is appropriate. Transfers on the basis of personal relationships shall be made in accordance with existing transfer procedures, but in any case, the bureau Assistant Chief shall ensure immediate and appropriate action is taken to preclude the continuance of the personal relationship conflict in the chain of command or within a workgroup. TBP 2.12

3. If any supervisor has any indication that a personal relationship as defined in General Order 706.01 D4 exists or is developing between another supervisor and a subordinate which would violate General Order 706.02 A1, the supervisor shall ask reasonable questions relating to the matter as it involves the workplace. If it is determined that a conflict does exist, the action as described in General Order 706.02, A.2 above shall be taken. If it is determined a relationship exists and the supervisor involved in the relationship has not reported it as required by General Order 706.02 A.2, a disciplinary investigation will be initiated in accordance with existing procedures for such investigations.

4. An employee who has a personal relationship with any employee shall not contact any person within the department for the purpose of directly or indirectly influencing any decisions concerning that employee’s terms, conditions, or privileges of employment.

A. When personal, family, or business relationships between employees that create a conflict occur in the workplace, there is cause for concern by the department. These relationships must be addressed and resolved in the interest of maintaining a safe and productive working environment for all employees.
1. Any relationship that presents a conflict or proves to be detrimental to the safety and productivity of the work group is prohibited.

2. When a situation meeting the criteria in General Order 706.03.A.1 exists, the supervisor of the involved employees shall document the conflict or detrimental actions and results in an Interoffice Communication and forward this IOC up the chain of command to the appropriate division commander or manager. If the division commander or manager concurs with the assessment, the commander/manager shall ensure one of the involved employees is immediately reassigned to a position in which the conflict no longer exists. The bureau Assistant Chief shall be notified to ensure the action taken is appropriate. Transfers shall be made in accordance with existing transfer procedures, but in any case, the bureau Assistant Chief shall ensure immediate and appropriate action is taken to preclude the continuance of the conflict within a workgroup.
3. Transfers approved by the Chief of Police under this section shall not be subject to the grievance procedure.
A. A family member shall not occupy a position which could affect another family member’s employment, conditions or terms of employment, or other management-related personnel action. TBP 2.12

1. If a family relationship exists or occurs between a supervisor and subordinate who are within a two-rank separation in the same chain of command or workgroup, the supervisor shall immediately inform their commander or manager. The commander or manager shall ensure one of the involved employees is immediately reassigned so that the supervisor/subordinate relationship conflict no longer exists. The bureau Assistant Chief shall be notified to ensure the action taken is appropriate. Transfers on the basis of family relationship conflicts shall be made in accordance with existing transfer procedures but, in any case, the bureau Assistant Chief shall ensure immediate and appropriate action is taken to preclude continuation of the family relationship conflict in the chain of command.

2. An employee who has a family relationship with any employee shall not contact any person within the department for the purpose of directly or indirectly influencing any decisions concerning that employee’s terms, conditions or privileges of employment.

3. If a family relationship exists or occurs between two (2) employees in a workgroup who are not a supervisor and subordinate, but still falls within the two-rank separation, the employees shall immediately inform their supervisor. The supervisor, with concurrence of their commander or manager, shall ensure one of the involved employees is immediately reassigned so that the family relationship conflict no longer exists. The bureau Assistant Chief shall be notified to ensure the action taken is appropriate. Transfers on the basis of family relationship conflicts shall be made in accordance with existing transfer procedures but, in any case, the bureau Assistant Chief shall ensure immediate and appropriate action is taken to preclude continuation of the family relationship conflict.

4. If the workgroup division or section is large enough to permit the officers to work in different areas or times with minimal interaction, the employees may be permitted to work within that division or section with the concurrence and written permission of their chain of command up to the level of the bureau Assistant Chief.
A. Public trust requires that employees avoid even the appearance of a conflict between their professional responsibilities and their personal business interests. TBP 2.12

1. Supervisors shall not enter into or continue a business relationship with members of their chain of command. If a pre-existing business relationship exists or should a transfer create a business relationship conflict, the involved supervisor shall immediately inform their commander or manager. The commander or manager shall ensure one of the involved employees is immediately reassigned so that the supervisor/subordinate business relationship no longer exists. The concerned bureau assistant chief shall be notified to ensure the action taken is appropriate. Transfers on the basis of business relationship conflicts shall be made in accordance with existing transfer procedures but, in any case, the bureau assistant chief shall ensure immediate and appropriate action is taken to preclude continuation of the business relationship conflict in the chain of command.

2. Any employee who has a business relationship with any other employee shall not contact any person within the department for the purpose of directly or indirectly influencing any decisions concerning that employee’s terms, conditions, or privileges of employment.
3. No employee shall have a business relationship with any company or person that does or seeks to do business with the city.

items.t: EMPLOYEE APPLICANTS, TRAINEES, AND PROBATIONARY EMPLOYEES
l: A. Employee applicants, trainees, and probationary employees in their selection, employment and training are especially vulnerable to implied threats or coercion, as they are constantly being evaluated.

1. Regular and permanent employees are in a position to exert influence over and may participate in some way in the selection, training or evaluation of employee applicants, trainees, or probationary employees. Therefore, any personal or business relationship with any applicant, trainee, or probationary employee is prohibited.

2. Employees who have a pre-existing personal, family, or business relationship with an applicant, trainee, or probationary employee shall refrain from making any decisions regarding the application, selection, training, or probationary employee status of the individual. Employees who have such a pre-existing personal, family, or business relationship shall immediately inform their commander or manager. The commander or manager shall ensure that the involved employee makes no decisions that may directly or indirectly affect the application, selection, trainee, or probationary employee/officer process.

3. Employees who do share a personal, family, or business relationship with any employee applicant, trainee, a probationary officer or employee shall not contact any person within the department or any person involved in the selection, training, or evaluation process for the purpose of directly or indirectly influencing any decisions concerning the subject individual’s terms, conditions, or privileges of employment.
4. Employees who are in their entry-level trainee or probationary status are prohibited from establishing a personal or business relationship with any other employee of the department. TBP 2.12

5. Employees who are in their entry-level trainee or probationary status shall immediately report to their division commander or manager any actions by any regular or permanent employee which they perceive as an effort to initiate a business or personal relationship. TBP 2.12
